Hand-compiled 2026-07-30 by reading research/experiments.md and research/open_questions.md for explicit ROOT VALIDATION LADDER gate-status language (CLAUDE.md defines gates 1-5: DATA/SIGNAL/LOGIC/SIZING/EXECUTION). Every entry carries a source_ref pointing at the file/line or session date the status came from, so a human or a future session can re-verify rather than trust this file blindly — same discipline as entity_map.json's provenance notes. This is a SNAPSHOT, not a live feed: it reflects the ladder position as of last_update_date per root and goes stale as new gate runs land; a future session should re-run the compilation (or extend it) periodically, not treat it as self-updating. RAW overlays (status raw_only, current_gate 0) make no predictive claim by design — the ladder does not apply to them, they are not 'behind' signal roots that failed a gate. Status values: raw_only, gate1_pending, gate1_pass, gate1_fail, gate2_pending, gate2_pass, gate2_fail, gate3_pass, gate4_pass, gate5_pass, killed. OPTIONAL 'readiness_trigger' field (added 2026-08-13, EDGE DOCTRINE #3 compile-knowledge-into-code): on a gateN_pending root whose research/ NEXT note already states a concrete, dated re-run condition (not a vague 'wait and see'), encodes that condition machine-readably so scripts/ladder_readiness_check.py can answer 'is this root unblocked yet' without a session re-deriving it from prose — the exact condition dozens of sessions have manually re-grepped/re-stated for usaspending_contracts/cftc_cot_positioning/sec_8k_earnings_language alone. Types: {type:'date', not_before: ISO date} — a flat calendar threshold; {type:'archive_days', since: ISO date, min_days: N} — N calendar days must elapse since a pipeline's own gate-1 ship/archive-start date; {type:'weekly_reports', since: ISO date, min_count: N, cadence_days: 7} — an ESTIMATE by elapsed time assuming the stated cadence holds (real holiday/skip gaps can shift the true count — the checker flags this type as an estimate, not a live-verified fact). Every readiness_trigger carries source_note reproducing the exact research/ NEXT-note language it encodes, so the number can be re-verified against prose, not trusted blindly. This field is added ONLY where an explicit prior session already committed to the exact condition in writing — never invented fresh by the compiling session. OPTIONAL 'detail_route' field (added 2026-08-16): on a root that has grown its own dedicated live /data page beyond this ladder listing (gate2_pass or further), the app hash route to that page, so signalLadder.tsx can render a 'view live signal' link generically instead of a per-root hardcoded special case. roots.note: GATE 1 stays PASSED (v1.0.552, unaffected). The general 'leveraged-money extremes mean-revert across financial futures' hypothesis, AS STATED, is REJECTED — where a Bonferroni-surviving effect exists it is asset-specific and directionally inconsistent, not the one coherent mechanism the hypothesis proposed. The TLT momentum finding is filed as its own distinct, un-pre-registered candidate (needs a disjoint out-of-sample window before any trust, same discipline as the 2026-08-03 OCC reversal candidate) rather than promoted here. Dealer-side positioning (cftcTff.ts's own 'informed side' docstring hypothesis) remains untested, a separate un-pre-registered hypothesis for a future session. roots.name: FINRA daily short-volume (4-facility CNMS reconstruction)
roots.note: GATE 1 PASSED 2026-07-05 (100.000% sum-of-parts identity across 12,240 symbols vs FINRA's own 4 independent per-facility files). GATE 2 FIRST-PASS RUN 2026-08-06 (scripts/finra_shortvol_gate2.ts): FAIL against the pre-registered composite bar — day-clustered HIGH_SHORT/NEUTRAL/LOW_SHORT buckets, 16 weekly Wednesdays 2026-01-07..2026-04-22. The +20d HIGH-LOW spread alone clears significance (t=2.279 > crit=2.131, df=15) but the required monotonic ordering fails: NEUTRAL underperforms LOW_SHORT at both horizons (a U-shape, not a gradient) — per Reasoning Standard #4 the composite bar governs, not the significant piece alone. PRE-REGISTERED FOLLOW-UP RETEST 2026-08-15 (scripts/finra_shortvol_gate2_retest.ts), IDENTICAL 16-day window, two changes only: HIGH_SHORT tested against a full-population-proxy baseline (systematic alphabetical sample, not the rank-centered NEUTRAL band) instead of the 3-bucket ordering design; VXX-ratio/SPY-vs-MA50 regime classification mirrored from ml_model_v2.py added. Result: the +20d HIGH-vs-population day-clustered spread SHRINKS to +1.561% (t=1.303, df=15, crit=2.131 — does not clear significance), down from the first run's +2.244% HIGH-vs-LOW spread (t=2.279, which did clear significance alone) — this explains the first run's U-shape (NEUTRAL was itself an unusually poor-performing band relative to the broader population, inflating the HIGH-LOW contrast) rather than confirming a real HIGH_SHORT edge. Sign was stable across the two regimes with ≥3 sample days (bull +3.091%/n=3, neutral +1.680%/n=12; bear n=1, too few days to count) so the regime half of the pre-stated bar passed, but the composite bar requires BOTH clauses — VERDICT FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE. NOT marked killed: both tests share the same 16-day window (2026-01-07..2026-04-22), so this is a corrected re-analysis of the same period, not a disjoint out-of-sample replication or a sign-reversal — the repo's own kill precedent (occ_options_volume/cftc_tff_positioning/jodi_oil_stocks) requires one of those two. Two consecutive fails on the same window (an ordering fail, then a significance fail under an unbiased baseline) substantially lowers the prior for a real standalone edge in this exact operationalization; a future session closing this permanently should run a genuinely disjoint out-of-sample window (e.g. 2026-05 onward, now available) rather than re-testing 2026-01..04 a third way.

roots.name: Wikimedia pageviews (retail-attention proxy, pytrends replacement)
roots.note: GATE 1 (DATA) PASS, run for the first time this session per the module's own pre-stated bar ('views vs known events, e.g. earnings dates, on 10 hand-checked tickers'): 11/11 hand-checked tickers show pageviews peaking above their own trailing baseline in the [SEC 8-K Item 2.02 filing date, +1] window (ratios 1.06x-3.46x, all directionally consistent; 4/11 clear 1.5x). Found and fixed a real defect while building the check: scripts/wikiattention_gate1.ts's PART A (live redirect-safety scan, now re-runnable) caught 3 of 22 seed pairs (PLTR/AMC/SMCI) pointed at Wikipedia REDIRECT STUB titles the pageviews API doesn't follow -- AMC was serving ~1% of the real article's traffic (8 vs 750 views/day), a 94x undercount, since the pipeline went live 2026-07-05. Corrected in datacore/wiki_articles.json, pinned in server/wikiAttention.test.ts. UPDATE 2026-09-04 (scheduled-routine PRODUCT session, same UTC day): GATE 2 attempted for the first time, against REAL data (scripts/wikiattention_gate2.py). 23 seed tickers x 516 real trading days, pooled per pre-registered cap-tier split. RESULT: forward volume_ratio held and cleared a Bonferroni bar at every horizon in both groups (small/mid-cap effect ~2x mega-cap's, matching the predicted asymmetry); realized_vol did not hold. NOT PROMOTED that session: the volume finding was UNCONTROLLED for the confound the hypothesis's own header names as the interesting case -- 'attention without news' -- a same-day 8-K (or other news event) could drive both the pageview spike and the volume spike independently. UPDATE 2026-09-04 (fourth scheduled-routine session this UTC day) -- THE NEWS-FREE CONTROL, GATE 2 PROMOTED: scripts/wikiattention_gate2_newsfree.py built and run live against real data (the exact control the prior session named as its own NEXT). Per-ticker EDGAR 8-K filing dates (ANY 8-K, not just Item-2.02 -- the broader bar the prior session's NEXT note specified) fetched live from data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK##########.json for all 23 seed tickers (CIK resolved via sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json); coverage confirmed to reach the full ~2-year lookback for every ticker (edgar_coverage_incomplete_tickers: []). Spike days with an 8-K filed on the spike day itself or the trading day before it were excluded from the SAMPLE side only -- the baseline (all non-spike days) is unchanged from the original design, so this is a direct extension of the prior test, not a redefinition. RESULT: 109 of 366 small/mid-cap spike-days (~30%) and 17 of 86 mega-cap spike-days (~20%) were excluded as news-contaminated. The volume effect SHRANK (as expected -- some of the original signal really was news-coincidence) but SURVIVED the pre-registered Bonferroni bar (alpha/10=0.005) at every horizon for the PRIMARY small/mid-cap group: h=1 mean 1.279x vs baseline 1.039x (diff 0.240, was 0.426 unfiltered -- 56% of the original effect survives), p<0.0001; h=3 mean 1.226x vs 1.053x (diff 0.173, was 0.255 -- 68% survives), p<0.0001; h=5 mean 1.195x vs 1.063x (diff 0.133, was 0.181 -- 74% survives), p=0.0014. The secondary mega-cap comparison group is WEAKER and mixed as expected (structurally more-arbitraged attention, per EDGE DOCTRINE #2): h=1 p=0.0083 (misses the 0.005 bar), h=3 p=0.0050 (exactly at the bar), h=5 p=0.0023 (clears) -- consistent with 'weaker, not a clean pass' for the secondary group, which the pre-registered hypothesis never required to pass on its own. HONESTY CAVEAT carried forward, not hidden: the per-ticker sign-consistency robustness check that corroborated the unfiltered result (21/23 tickers positive, p=6.6e-5) is WEAKER here -- only 11/16 small/mid tickers with an adequate news-free sample (n>=5) show mean>baseline at h=3 (binomial p=0.21, not itself significant), most plausibly because per-ticker news-free spike counts shrank to single digits for several tickers (a power loss from the filter, not necessarily a different true effect) rather than the pooled test being driven by a handful of outliers -- flagged as an open question for a future session with more archive depth, not resolved here. VERDICT (per the pre-registered rule in the control script's own docstring): the PRIMARY pre-registered composite test (small/mid-cap pooled volume_ratio) survives the control at every horizon -- PROMOTED to gate2_pass for the VOLUME channel specifically (elevated forward trading volume in small/mid-cap names following an attention spike, net of same-day-or-prior-day 8-K filings). The REALIZED-VOLATILITY channel stays unproven (never significant, filtered or not) and NO DIRECTIONAL PRICE claim is made or implied -- gate 2 tests predictive power with no trading involved, per the ladder's own definition; GATE 3 (LOGIC: does a backtestable entry/exit rule built on this signal beat a same-universe/same-holding-period random-entry base rate net of costs) is a separate, not-yet-attempted step, and the sign-test weakening above is exactly the kind of thing a GATE 3 attempt should re-examine before trusting per-ticker generalization. Full pooled/per-ticker numbers, both sessions' full accounts, and gates in research/open_questions.md's 2026-09-04 WIKIMEDIA PAGEVIEWS GATE 2 and NEWS-FREE CONTROL entries. UPDATE 2026-09-05 (scheduled-routine [PRODUCT] session): shipped the first live SIGNAL surface for this root, mirroring gnss_integrity_adsb's own precedent -- server/wikiAttentionSignal.ts (a live z-score board over this repo's own rolling pageviews archive; the validated news-free-controlled result table above is carried as frozen constants, not recomputed per request) + /api/data/wiki-attention-signal + client/src/pages/wikiAttentionSignal.tsx (#/data/wiki-attention-signal, wired under the attention layer row in datamap.tsx same as gnss-integrity under aircraft). The live board does NOT re-check today's spikes against EDGAR (no live per-spike news-free classification) -- stated as an explicit caveat on the page itself, not silently assumed clean. Also corrected two now-stale 'no spike claims until gate 2 runs' comments/notes in server/routes.ts's RAW /api/data/attention route and its v1 mirror (both intentionally stay RAW-only per the RAW OVERLAYS vs SIGNALS rule; the old wording just implied gate 2 had not yet been attempted). Gate status unchanged by this session -- pure /data surface addition over the already gate2_pass computation, same scope as gnss_integrity_adsb's 2026-08-24 API-surface session. NEXT: a v1 keyed mirror of this endpoint (same shape as gnss-integrity-signal's own v1 mirror) plus an apiProduct.ts LICENSE_MARKS entry and agent tool, if this root is ever monetized; GATE 3 (backtested entry/exit rule) remains the ladder's own next step and is unaffected by this UI/API-surface change. UPDATE 2026-09-05 (second scheduled-routine [PRODUCT] session, same UTC day): the v1 keyed mirror named above as NEXT shipped -- /api/v1/data/wiki-attention-signal (server/routes.ts, reuses computeWikiAttentionSignal() directly, no new computation/poller) plus LICENSE_MARKS['data/wiki-attention-signal']/apiMeta() endpoint entry/voltrade_wiki_attention_signal agent tool/RESPONSE_DATA_SCHEMAS entry (server/apiProduct.ts), same structural pattern as gnss-integrity-signal's own v1 mirror. Gate status unchanged -- pure API-surface addition over the already gate2_pass computation. UPDATE 2026-09-05 (third scheduled-routine [RESEARCH] session, same UTC day) -- GATE 3 (LOGIC) ATTEMPTED, NOT PASSED: scripts/wikiattention_gate3.py built and run live against real data, testing the one question gate 2 left open -- can a simple entry/exit rule built on the validated news-free attention-spike signal beat a same-universe random-entry base rate, net of costs (system_config.py's own SLIPPAGE_ILLIQUID/SLIPPAGE_PCT constants, not invented figures)? PRE-REGISTERED RULE (one, chosen before any result seen): long-only, buy at the news-free spike day's close, sell at close h={1,3,5} days later -- the simplest rule gate 2's own finding (elevated forward VOLUME only, no direction, no volatility) could support. PRE-REGISTERED PRIOR: LOW (~15-20%), reasoned from gate 2's own scope (a volume finding is not a direction finding) plus the Barber & Odean (2008) retail-attention literature's documented reversal-not-continuation pattern plus real round-trip costs (0.40% small/mid-cap) being large relative to plausible short-horizon effects. RESULT: WIKIMEDIA'S OWN API RATE LIMIT (429s, affecting a different random ticker subset on every one of 4 independent live attempts this session despite spacing from 0.6s up to 10s/ticker) prevented full 23-ticker coverage in any single run -- an honest coverage limitation, not a data-availability one (11 of 19 small/mid seed tickers were fetched successfully at least once across the 4 attempts). Rather than trust one partial draw, all 4 independent partial-coverage pooled runs were compared: p-values for the primary small/mid-cap pooled forward-return effect ranged 0.24-0.99 across horizons and draws, NEVER approaching the pre-registered Bonferroni bar (alpha/3=0.0167) in any draw, and the sign of the point estimate FLIPPED between draws (9-ticker draw: mean_diff -0.0003/-0.0029/-0.0002 at h=1/3/5; 6-ticker draw, 5 overlapping: +0.0045/+0.007/+0.0106; a 2-ticker OKLO+JOBY draw: strongly negative) -- sign-instability across independent resamples of the same underlying signal is itself evidence of a genuine null, not a real but underpowered effect. VERDICT PER THE PRE-REGISTERED RULE: GATE 3 NOT PASSED for this exact spec -- wikimedia_pageviews_attention's validated VOLUME signal (gate2_pass, unchanged) does not translate into a naive long-only directional edge net of costs. Fault localized to the LOGIC layer specifically (DATA and SIGNAL both already verified) -- does not call gate 1/2 into question, does not demote current_gate/status (both stay 2/gate2_pass: the live /data signal board and v1 API mirror remain valid SIGNAL-layer surfaces, now with an honest 'attempted and not tradeable' footnote). Full account and all 4 draws' numbers in research/open_questions.md's 2026-09-05 WIKIMEDIA PAGEVIEWS GATE 3 entry. NEXT: this exact long-only spec is closed, not to be re-attempted without new evidence; a future session could pre-register a genuinely different rule (e.g. conditioning entry direction on the spike day's own realized return, a momentum-vs-reversal question this session named but did NOT test, REASONING STANDARD #4) as a separate, freshly-pre-registered experiment.

roots.note: GATE 1 (DATA) ground-truth check run this session against server/fdicBanks.ts's own documented ladder path ('gate 1 = cross-check a failure's QBFASSET/QBFDEP vs the FDIC press release'). Sampled the 4 most recent failures live from api.fdic.gov/banks/failures and cross-checked each against (a) the institution's own FDIC Call Report history (api.fdic.gov/banks/financials) and (b) the FDIC's own press release text where fetchable. 3 of 4 EXACT matches to a Call Report on file: Metropolitan Capital B&T (CERT 57488) QBFASSET/QBFDEP 261185/212152 match its 2025-09-30 Call Report exactly AND match the FDIC press release's own stated figures verbatim ('As of September 30, 2025 ... total assets of $261.1 million and total deposits of $212.1 million'); COST 19647 matches the press release's '$19.7 million' DIF estimate. Santa Anna National Bank (CERT 5520) 76938/71376 matches its 2025-03-31 Call Report exactly. Pulaski Savings Bank (CERT 28611) 49466/42741 matches its 2024-09-30 Call Report exactly. ONE MISMATCH, honestly not glossed over: Community Bank and Trust - West Georgia (CERT 25796, the single most recent failure, 2026-05-01) shows QBFASSET/QBFDEP 305716/296420, which does NOT match its last Call Report on file (2025-12-31: 288221/268292, which IS what the FDIC press release itself cites verbatim -- 'As of December 31, 2025 ... total assets of $288 million and total deposits of $268 million') or any earlier quarter. Best-evidenced explanation (not confirmed): FDIC's public financials bulk index (risview snapshot, createTimestamp 2026-06-08) may not yet carry a final pre-failure Call Report the failures endpoint's own record already reflects -- consistent with this being the ONLY sampled failure recent enough for that lag to apply, not a defect in this feed's parsing (parseFailures() just relays FDIC's own field values unchanged, verified by reading server/fdicBanks.ts this session). COST also separately confirmed honest: West Georgia's COST is still null in FDIC's live API today (2026-08-18), over 3 months after the 2026-05-01 press release stated a preliminary $97M DIF estimate -- confirms FDIC's own machine-readable COST field lags its own press releases significantly, validating (not just assuming) the module's existing never-coerce-null-to-zero design decision. VERDICT: DATA gate PASSED -- the feed faithfully relays real, externally-verifiable FDIC figures; the one discrepancy is a known, honestly-logged open question about recency lag, not evidence of parsing or archival corruption. Gate 2 (SIGNAL -- failure events vs forward KRE/regional-bank returns) NOT attempted this session (no live market-data access in this sandbox: ALPACA_KEY/ALPACA_SECRET absent, Yahoo query1 429s, yfinance not installed) and separately blocked on the still-undone ticker/entity-graph join this root has never had (most failed institutions are small non-public regional banks) -- both real, not this session's scope. GET /api/diag/fdic_gate2?since=2022-01-01&horizons=5,10,20: n_failure_events_fetched=13, n_kre_bars=1172. All three horizons FAILED the pre-committed 95% bootstrap significance bar (signal_detected:false, insufficient_n:false at every horizon -- 13 clears the module's own 5-event floor): 5d event_mean=-1.247% vs base_rate=+0.106% (p=0.208, CI [-2.02%,+2.28%]); 10d event_mean=-1.083% vs base_rate=+0.043% (p=0.4395, CI [-2.70%,+3.03%]); 20d event_mean=-0.305% vs base_rate=+0.148% (p=0.818, CI [-3.47%,+4.26%]). Matches the PRIOR stated in the 2026-09-03 build session before this probe existed (expected failures too sparse/telegraphed for a clean signal). Directionally the event mean is negative at all three horizons while the base rate is positive, and both the p-value and |event mean| shrink monotonically as the horizon lengthens -- consistent with a short-lived correlated dip reverting toward the base rate, not a persistent lead/lag relationship -- but neither observation clears the pre-registered bar, and treating a p=0.21 non-result as a promising negative correlation would be exactly the after-the-fact-story failure REASONING STANDARD #4/#10 exist to prevent. VERDICT: GATE 2 FAILED, logged per ROOT VALIDATION LADDER (fails a gate = logged at its layer of death, gates may not be skipped regardless of how promising they looked). GATE 1 (DATA) is unaffected and remains PASSED -- the failures feed itself is still accurate; the KRE-forward-return hypothesis on top of it is what did not clear its bar. roots.name: Gas flare candidates (persistent-hotspot VIIRS FIRMS detector, free alternative to VIIRS Nightfire)
roots.note: Built earlier the same day (server/gasFlareCandidates.ts, v1.0.826) with GATE 1 designed but not run ('no production archive access in this sandbox'). This session had live DIAG_TOKEN production access and ran it (scripts/gasflare_gate1.ts): per-country candidate-count density (default detector thresholds, minNights=3/minPersistence=0.5) vs the World Bank 2026 Global Gas Flaring Tracker Report's published country order (Russia, Iran, Iraq, Venezuela, Mexico, Libya, Algeria, Nigeria, US), web-searched this session. SCOPE CUT: Russia excluded (its admin0 polygon crosses the antimeridian, so a bbox query for it is effectively the whole globe at 41-81N and truncates at the archive probe's 5000-row/day cap on ordinary wildfire noise -- confirmed live, not assumed) -- n=8, ranks 2-9 of the published 9. RESULT: Spearman rho = -0.4762 against the pre-registered critical value +0.738 (n=8, alpha=0.05) -- GATE 1 FAIL, and the sign is negative, not just non-significant. Real per-country candidate counts (2026-08-15..28, 14-day window chosen to sit clear of the KNOWN BROKEN #37 vessel-archive anomaly window on general principle): USA 192 (highest of the 8, despite ranking LOWEST of the 8 by published volume; 10/14 days truncated at 5000 rows -- strong evidence of western-US wildfire-season contamination the persistence filter did not exclude), Algeria 111, Libya 79, Venezuela 62, Mexico 45, Iraq 6, Iran 0, Nigeria 0. Robustness check (exploratory, not the pre-registered test): excluding the USA outlier, rho is still negative (-0.214) on the remaining 7 -- this is not solely a single-country artifact. DIAGNOSIS: the grid+persistence method alone does not adequately separate large, slow-moving/re-igniting wildfire complexes from true flare stacks at country-aggregate scale; Iran's zero count (the region's #1 remaining flarer) suggests a separate miss (known flare sites not clearing the persistence/grid parameters as tuned, or a real archive-coverage gap for that bbox/window -- not diagnosed further this session). NEXT (1) attempted same day, later session: a wildfire-discriminator refinement (frpCV, coefficient of variation of a site's per-night mean FRP, added as an opt-in maxFrpCV filter to findGasFlareCandidates(), grounded in VIIRS Nightfire's own published methodology of separating flares from wildfires on 'temperature and persistence' -- flares hold a stable radiant output, wildfires are far more variable; FRP is the nearest available proxy since this module has no Planck-fit temperature). Threshold maxFrpCV=0.6 was chosen a priori from that qualitative claim, not fit to this dataset. RE-RUN against the identical 2026-08-15..28 archive rows: refined candidate counts shrank materially in every country (USA 192->156, Algeria 111->86, Libya 79->71, Venezuela 62->40, Mexico 45->33; Iraq/Iran/Nigeria unchanged at 6/0/0) but the RANK ORDER did not move at all -- Spearman rho stayed exactly -0.4762, identical to 4 decimal places, because the filter thinned every country roughly proportionally rather than correcting USA's specific over-representation relative to its (lowest-of-8) published rank. CLEAN NEGATIVE for this exact refinement, reported per MEASUREMENT INTEGRITY rather than re-tried with a second threshold in the same session (REASONING STANDARD #4). Per the module's own HONESTY CLAUSE, this was the one refinement attempt the prior note reserved before recommending VIIRS Nightfire's free registration -- that ask is now the honest next step (filed in research/wishlist.md), though (2) Iran's zero count and (3) the Russia antimeridian query remain untried and could still change the picture before spending a registration ask. Full account: research/open_questions.md GAS FLARE CANDIDATES entry, 2026-09-01 second addendum. UPDATE 2026-09-03 (scheduled-routine [PRODUCT] session): both remaining NEXT items attempted. (1) Russia antimeridian query BUILT (server/countryLookup.ts's new countryBboxParams(), splits a dateline-crossing country into 2 tight bboxes instead of 1 globe-spanning one) and RUN -- full n=9 truth rank, critical rho recomputed EXACTLY via full permutation (0.7000 at n=9, cross-checked against the standing n=8 pin 0.7381 before trusting it). RESULT: baseline rho -0.4667, refined rho -0.5 -- still GATE1_FAIL, same negative direction. Russia itself is a NEW finding: only 6 candidates (rank 6 of 9 in our own ordering, not 1st) with 14/14 days truncated at the archive probe's 5000-row/day cap -- the antimeridian fix is verified correct (unit-tested), but Russia's main-landmass bbox alone still spans the whole breadth of Eurasia and saturates the per-day cap on ordinary boreal background detections before flare signal survives; a genuine measurement limitation (would need oblast-level sub-bboxing), not a detector or fix defect. (2) Iran's zero-candidate count ROOT-CAUSED, not just re-observed: only 165 of 3,726 fetched rows (4.4%) are nighttime-tagged, spanning just 3 of the 14 window nights -- vs Libya's 3,545/5,520 (64%) spanning 14/14 nights, confirming this is Iran-specific coverage sparsity, not a global archive daynight-tagging bug or a detector-logic miss (loosened thresholds DO surface candidates at geographically real Iranian flare sites -- Ahvaz/Khuzestan, South Pars/Assaluyeh -- once the 3-night ceiling is relaxed). WHY Iran's nighttime FIRMS coverage is this sparse in this window (VIIRS overpass geometry vs an archive gap vs a seasonal artifact) is NOT resolved this session -- filed as open. Root-level disposition unchanged: 3 independent negative correlation runs now on record (n=8 baseline/refined, n=9 baseline/refined); NEXT step recommendation is the already-filed VIIRS Nightfire free-registration ask (wishlist.md) over further patching of this free alternative, per this update's own full account.
